# CreateLight

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Lights](Blitz3D-Lights)

</div>


```blitzbasic
CreateLight:Int32 type:Int32=1, parent:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | In | Int32 | `1` | 1 for a directional light, 2 for a point light, 3 for a spot light. Defaults to 1. |
| `parent` | In | Int32 | `0` | Entity the light follows, or 0 for none. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns:** The handle of the new light.

## Description

Creates a light and returns its handle. Without a light everything in the world is lit only by [AmbientLight](AmbientLight), which looks flat. A light is an entity: position and rotation work like on any other entity.

* **1, directional** (the default) is like the sun. Only its rotation matters, it shines along its own forward direction (+Z) and has no position or range.
* **2, point** is like a light bulb. It shines in all directions from its position and fades out until its range.
* **3, spot** is a cone of light that shines along its forward direction (+Z). See [LightConeAngles](LightConeAngles).

A new light is white, sits at the origin and has a range of 1000. Any other value for `type` creates a directional light. Only the 8 lights that come first in the world affect a frame, so plan with 8 at most.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
PositionEntity camera, 0, 0, -5
AmbientLight 20, 20, 20
; A point light to the left of the ball.
light = CreateLight(2)
PositionEntity light, -3, 2, -2
LightRange light, 12
ball = CreateSphere(24)
EntityColor ball, 230, 230, 230
RenderWorld
Flip
WaitKey
```
